title: Smoked Sausage Platter
shortDescription: Mixed links with peppers, onions, and mustard bar for ten
subtitle: Mixed links with peppers, onions, and mustard bar for ten
description: A mix of smoked sausages—kielbasa, andouille, and sweet Italian—slow-smoke alongside peppers and onions until snappy and juicy. Serve on a platter with mustards, buns, and sauerkraut for build-your-own plates.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Sausage Platter in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep links and vegetables
steps.instruction: Score each sausage lightly on two sides. Toss peppers and onions with olive oil, smoked paprika, and salt until evenly coated and lightly glossy.

steps.title: Smoke the sausage
steps.instruction: Heat smoker to 275°F. Arrange links with space between each piece and smoke until internal temperature reaches 165°F and casings snap when bent, about 45–60 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 275°F.

steps.title: Cook the pepper mixture
steps.instruction: During the last 30 minutes, cook peppers and onions in a cast-iron pan on the smoker until softened and lightly charred at the edges. Target oven/smoker temperature: 275°F.

steps.title: Warm the sauerkraut
steps.instruction: Heat sauerkraut in a small saucepan with a splash of beer or broth until steaming. Keep warm on the sideboard away from direct heat so it does not dry out.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Smoked Sausage Platter onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Build the platter
steps.instruction: Pile links on a board with pepper-onion mix, sauerkraut, rolls, and a mustard bar. Verify every link hits at least 165°F before calling the meal ready.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Smoked Sausage Platter — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Mix link types for variety—one spicy, one smoky, one sweet keeps the platter interesting.
Hold links in a foil-lined pan with a splash of beer to stay juicy if service delays.
Add pickled jalapeños to the bar for crews that want heat without touching the smoker settings.
tonightSpread: Full sausage board with mustards, peppers, onions, kraut, and toasted rolls.
Quick potato salad and chips for a classic cookout spread that needs no extra oven time.
leftovers: Slice links into a breakfast scramble with peppers and cheddar.
Chop and simmer in marinara for a fast smoky pasta sauce on the next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sausage platters feed fast with almost zero knife work. Links forgive timing, reheat well, and let picky eaters choose their own adventure with toppings.
mealPrepNotes: Score links lightly so smoke penetrates without splitting open. Slice peppers and onions the night before into labeled bins. Mustard bar can be set up 30 minutes before service.
